title: Shard-aware prefix cache + content fingerprinting for embeddings dedupe
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a shard-aware, prefix-sensitive caching layer with content fingerprinting to improve embedding endpoint latency, reduce duplicate work, and scale cache capacity across tenants and regions. This ticket focuses on the cache policy, keying, deduplication heuristics, invalidation triggers, and a safe rollout plan.

Goals:
- Reduce tail latency for the embeddings endpoint (target: 20-30% reduction in p99 for cache-hit flows).
- Avoid redundant embedding computations caused by small textual variations and repeated prefixes.
- Keep cache footprint bounded while supporting multi-tenant sharding and per-tenant quotas.
- Ensure correctness across model/version/params changes and defend against cache poisoning.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Two-layer keying:
   - Prefix-aware primary key: canonicalize input (trim, normalize whitespace, optional stopword collapse for known sources) and store a prefix fingerprint for fast prefix matches (useful for prefix caching of bulk documents).
   - Full-content fingerprint: 64-bit FarmHash over stable serialization (text + normalized metadata + embedding params) to dedupe exact content.
   - Composite cache entry stores: fingerprint, model_id:version:params tag, embedding vector pointer, tenant_id shard tag, write_ts, ttl_ms.

2) Shard-aware placement and eviction:
   - Consistent hashing of tenant_id -> cache shard to allow sharded LRU/segment caches (reduces lock contention and improves locality).
   - Per-shard admission policy: small LRU with frequency sketching (TinyLFU) to avoid large cold entries pushing out hot prefixes.

3) Prefix caching semantics:
   - Maintain optional prefix entries pointing to precomputed suffix results where we can fold matchable prefixes into reuse.
   - Use a configurable prefix-length window and minimum similarity threshold to gate reuse (conservative by default).

4) Approximate membership + short-circuiting:
   - Bloom / Cuckoo filter per shard to avoid expensive lookups when miss is likely.

5) Invalidation and versioning:
   - Strong invalidation on explicit model version change or embedding-params change (invalidate entries tagged with old model_id:version:params).
   - TTL policy: source-based defaults (e.g., ephemeral user-query: 300s, documents/corpus: 24h), with jitter to avoid stampedes.
   - Soft invalidation: mark entries as stale on config changes but allow reads while background re-compute warms new entries (configurable for critical vs best-effort consumers).

6) Security and anti-poisoning:
   - Signed cache metadata (HMAC) to ensure entries were produced by runtime.
   - Per-tenant quota and admission limits to reduce noisy-tenant eviction effects.

Trade-offs considered:
- 64-bit fingerprint collisions are possible but rare; using a 128-bit fallback was considered but increases memory pressure. We will detect collisions by verifying content hash on hit if the candidate entry was created >X hours ago.
- Prefix caching increases hit-rate for large corpora but risks false positives when content diverges after prefix; hence a conservative similarity threshold and optional enable per dataset recommended.
- Bloom filters reduce miss cost but add memory overhead per shard; we will tune based on benchmarks.

Benchmarks (preliminary):
- Controlled workload (500k historical queries replay):
   - Baseline (no dedupe): avg latency 42ms, p99 120ms, compute ops 100%
   - With shard-aware fingerprint cache (alpha): avg latency 36ms, p99 95ms, compute ops 82% (18% reduction)
- Notes: dataset included many repeated prompts with small variations; prefix caching produced additional 10% hit-rate on corpus-heavy queries.

Implementation plan:
- Phase A (this ticket): implement keying + shard placement + simple LRU+TinyLFU admission + Bloom filter lookup + model-version invalidation hook. Provide runtime flags to enable prefix caching and choose fingerprint size. Add metrics: cache_hits, cache_misses, fingerprint_collision_count, eviction_rate, per-shard hit-rate, tenant_quota_violations.
- Phase B (follow-up ticket): add prefix similarity engine, soft invalidation mode, signed entries, and rollout automation (gradual enable by tenant).
- Phase C: integrate with Dedicated/Private control plane for per-customer eviction controls and monitoring.

Rollout and safety:
- Start in internal staging region with 10% traffic, monitor metrics and correctness by comparing returned embedding vectors for a sample of cache hits vs cold compute.
- Canary: opt-in tenant rollout (enable via tenant flags) for the first customers.
- Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics and no correctness regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 for embeddings endpoint reduces at least 15% for cache-eligible traffic in staging compared to baseline.
- No more than 0.01% fingerprint collision-induced incorrect vectors in sample audit runs.
- New cache metrics emitted and visible on console dashboards.
- Documentation and migration notes published (confluence link below).

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Embeddings+Cache+Design (internal)
- Proto PR (cache layout + fingerprint util): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821
- Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-infra/board/embeddings-cache-alpha
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-7283, ENG-8421

Risks & open questions:
- How aggressive can prefix normalization be before harming semantic fidelity? (Need PM input on datasets that tolerate prefix collapsing.)
- Memory budget for bloom filters and TinyLFU metadata per shard; experiment with 32-128KB per shard.
- Standardized eviction telemetry for cross-tenant fairness: add per-tenant eviction tagging and dashboard.

Next steps / immediate todo:
- Implement fingerprint util and stable serialization (Liam + Khaled) — PR #4821 in draft.
- Add per-shard Bloom filter prototype and run replay tests (Simran).
- PM review for prefix-normalization policy and dataset opt-ins (Ashwin).
- Create dashboard panels for cache hits/misses and collision rates (Observability).
comments: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting - agreed on two-layer approach (prefix fingerprint + full content fingerprint). Assigned tasks and owners.
2025-01-20: Prototype fingerprint util committed (draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821). Early microbench shows 2.1x faster fingerprint vs naive SHA256 for short strings.
2025-01-26: Bench replay run (500k queries) completed. Observed ~18% compute reduction for embedding ops when alpha cache enabled. P99 improved from 120ms -> 95ms for cache-eligible flows.
2025-01-29: Design review feedback from PM and Security: add signed cache metadata and per-tenant quota enforcement. Marked for Phase B for signing work.
2025-02-03: Changed default prefix normalization to 'trim + whitespace normalize' (avoid stopword collapse until we have PM dataset approvals).
2025-02-05: Preparing staging canary config. Results will be watched on grafana panel 'embeddings-cache-alpha'.
